## Goal

Document the herdr worklist hydrator in packages/herdr/README.md so operators understand its cadence, semantics, safety, and why pane-title IDs must survive truncation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. README documents: 30s cadence, immediate run on focus-resume, visibility gating (zero wl while hidden).
2. README documents demotion rules (in_review→completed, dependency-blocked→blocked, else→open) with the status/stage compatibility note.
3. README documents fail-open semantics (missing/unparseable CLI output → no demotions, never a crash).
4. README documents the pane-title ID-survival rationale (matching relies on ' - WL-<id>' in titles; pane-title amendment F0).
5. Docs match the shipped implementation (reviewed at close).

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/README.md

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add a 'Hydrator' subsection under the worklist/downtime worker docs area with the bullets above.

## Dependencies

- Requires F2 (implementation facts) and F0 (format rationale)

data.description:
## Goal

Wire the hydrator into the worklist plugin (packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts) as a TaskScheduler task, visibility-gated, with an immediate run when the tab regains focus (reusing the existing resume-poll machinery). No second interval loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A scheduler task id 'hydrate' is registered on the existing TaskScheduler with intervalMs 30_000, singleFlight: true, and runTimeoutMs set; a rejecting task never takes down the scheduler loop.
2. The hydrate task is visibility-gated: while the worklist pane is hidden it does not run and spawns zero wl processes (paneGate pattern).
3. On a hidden→visible transition, hydration runs immediately (in addition to the existing refresh) without waiting for the next 30s tick.
4. Hydrator deps are injected into worklist.ts (e.g. via opts) so tests can substitute fakes.
5. Full project suite passes; no regressions in existing worklist tests.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts — register hydrate task + resume hook
- packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts — reused as-is
- packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts — reuse PollGate/paneGate
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts — visibility-gated scheduler precedent

## Minimal Implementation

1. Register hydrate task alongside refresh/sync/resume-poll/downtime with the same interval/visibility wiring used by the downtime worker.
2. In the resume-poll hidden→visible transition branch, invoke the hydrate task immediately (parallel to the existing immediate refresh).

## Dependencies

- Requires F2 (hydrator module — runHydrationOnce to invoke)
data.title: Worklist: hydrate task + focus-resume

data.description:
## Goal

Implement the herdr hydrator module (packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts): every 30s (and on worklist focus-resume) it fetches all in_progress work items, matches each against work-item IDs in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace, and demotes any item with no matching pane per the signal-based rule (AC3 of parent WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI). Pure decision functions + orchestration with injectable deps; fail-open at every boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes) returns WL-[0-9A-Z]+ IDs found in pane labels.
2. isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes) returns true iff the ID appears in a running pane's label in any tab of the current workspace; workspace filtering via herdr pane list --workspace <id> / HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID env var.
3. decideDemotion(workItem, blockers): stage in_review → {status: completed, stage: in_review}; active outbound blocker (target not completed/deleted, stage not in_review/done, per isDependencyActive in packages/shared/src/database.ts) → {status: blocked, stage: plan_complete (or best compatible)}; else → {status: open, stage: intake_complete}; stage always chosen per src/config.ts compatibility.
4. runHydrationOnce(deps): fetches wl list --status in_progress, fetches panes, computes demotions, applies each via wl update (status+stage); an item with a matching pane is never touched.
5. Fail-open: wl/pane CLI missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output → skip the entire cycle with a log; the function never throws; no demotion happens on untrustworthy evidence.
6. All hydrator.test.ts tests pass; full project suite passes.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts — new module
- packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts — reuse runWl/extractJson/extractItems
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts — orchestration precedent
- src/commands/dep.ts + packages/shared/src/database.ts — dependency semantics (reference only)
- src/config.ts — status/stage compatibility (reference only)

## Minimal Implementation

1. Pure helpers: extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles, isActivePaneMatch, decideDemotion (status, stage) pair.
2. runHydrationOnce(deps) with injectable {runWl, runPaneList, now, log}; fetch in_progress; fetch panes filtered to workspace; outbound-edge stage fetch per blocker candidate (wl dep list carries status only — fetch stage via wl show for each edge not completed/deleted).
3. Apply demotions; wrap whole cycle in try/catch that logs and returns without demoting.

## Dependencies

- Requires F1 (hydrator.test.ts — written first; suite must pass to close)
- Requires F0 (pane-title format amendment — ID must survive truncation)
data.title: Hydrator: demote stale in_progress items

data.description:
The Herdr worklist selection list calls wl next to populate its results. wl next excludes dependency-blocked items by default (filterCandidates removes them unless includeBlocked is true). This means the Herdr selection list never shows dependency-blocked items, even though the user may need to see what is blocking their backlog.

Acceptance Criteria:
1. The Herdr worklist selection list includes dependency-blocked items alongside open and in-progress items.
2. Blocked items are rendered with a visible indicator (status icon) so their state is clear.
3. The change is confined to the fetchNextItems invocation in fetcher.ts - no other callers of wl next are affected.
4. Unit tests cover the new --include-blocked flag in the args array.

Notes:
The change adds --include-blocked to the wl next args in fetchNextItems() (packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts). status=blocked items were already included by wl next (the pipeline only penalises them with -10000); the gap is dependency-blocked items that are excluded entirely. Blocked items will rank low (penalised) by default scoring, so they appear at the bottom of the list.
data.title: Herdr selection list should show dependency-blocked items

data.description:
Inconsistency between the Herdr in_review stage filter and the ship release gate:

- The ship skill queries "wl list --stage in_review" with NO status filter (check-audit-gate.js, check-final-validation.js, generate-changelog.js), so a status=blocked item in the in_review stage (e.g. WL-0MTF5WO1N0088P5P) IS seen by the release gate and blocks the release.
- The Herdr in_review stage filter (fetchItemsByStage -> STAGE_STATUS.in_review = "completed,in-progress,open") EXCLUDES status=blocked items, so the same item never appears in the in_review filtered selection list.

The user-facing symptom: an in_review item that blocks the release is invisible in the /wl review view, so the selection list and the release gate disagree about what is in the review queue.

User story: As a Herdr user, I want the in_review filter to show every root item the ship release gate sees in in_review, so the selection list and the release gate agree on the review queue.

Acceptance Criteria:
1. fetchItemsByStage(in_review) issues a wl list query whose status filter includes blocked alongside completed/in-progress/open (verified by a unit test asserting the exec args).
2. A status=blocked root item at stage=in_review appears in the stage-filtered in_review list.
3. Other stages keep their existing status rules unchanged.
4. The stage-filter documentation (STAGE_STATUS comment in fetcher.ts, worklist.ts doc, packages/herdr/README.md) reflects that in_review includes blocked items.
5. Build passes and the herdr package test suite is green.

Notes:
- Root cause: STAGE_STATUS.in_review omits blocked. The project workflow (AGENTS.md, WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW) documented blocked as excluded, but the release gate does not exclude it — the exclusion makes release-blocking items invisible in the review filter.
- Fix: STAGE_STATUS.in_review = completed,in-progress,open,blocked. discovered-from:WL-0MV6TFX0600145M2
data.title: Herdr in_review filter hides blocked items that the release gate treats as release-blocking

data.description:
Follow-up to WL-0MV6TFX0600145M2. Adding --include-blocked to wl next made blocked items ELIGIBLE, but the default worklist still does not show a low-ranked blocked item such as WL-0MTF5WO1N0088P5P (status=blocked, stage=in_review, rank ~35 of 52):

- The base feed is `wl next -n <browseItemCount>` (default 20): the ranked #35 item is cut before it ever enters the pool.
- The mandatory subsets (critical, completed/in_review, in-progress) do not include status=blocked items, so smart selection cannot surface it either.
- Only the /wl review stage filter shows it (fixed in WL-0MV70XY6D008013C).

Per the operator: an in_review item blocks the release, so it must either appear in the list or not be in_review. It IS in_review, therefore it must appear in the DEFAULT list too.

User story: As a Herdr user, I want status=blocked root items always visible in the default worklist (like critical / in_review-completed / in-progress items), so release-blocking work can never be hidden by ranking or count caps.

Acceptance Criteria:
1. fetchMandatorySubsets() fetches status=blocked root-only items (wl list --status blocked --root-only) alongside the existing mandatory subsets.
2. selectWorkItems / isMandatoryItem treat status=blocked as mandatory: a blocked root item is always shown regardless of browseItemCount and rank.
3. The default worklist shows a low-ranked blocked in_review root item (regression test).
4. Non-blocked items keep existing behaviour (order, caps).
5. Build passes and the herdr package test suite is green.

Notes:
- discovered-from:WL-0MV6TFX0600145M2
- Also requires the user to close/reopen (or restart the herdr server to respawn) the worklist pane for new code to load: tsx runs without --watch, so an already-open pane keeps the old code.
